From: Tom Serrano <tom.serrano@elarahealth.com>

Cc: Elara Health Security <security@elarahealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions from security review after demo

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the demo earlier today. A couple of the security folks had targeted follow-ups so I wanted to capture them here and make sure we have answers we can share back with the InfoSec review board: 

- PII scope: what categories of customer data (names, emails, SSNs, medical identifiers) are written to Redwoods-managed storage vs only kept in memory/KV-cache?
- Retention: is there a configurable retention policy for generated responses and logs? what are the default and max retention windows?
- Residency: can we pin workloads to a US-only region (us-east-1) and ensure no cross-region backups?
- Support access / break-glass: what is the support access model? is there JIT/Elevated access for debugging, and what approvals & audit trail exist?
- Logging: do you provide raw request/response logs (redacted) and can those be exported to our SIEM?

We also have a standard security questionnaire — I can attach if it helps (I attached the questionnaire to this email).

Goal: get a concise one-page summary + any evidence (SOC2 summary, audit log samples) we can include in the board packet by Wednesday.

- Tom
Tom Serrano
Director, Security Operations | Elara Health
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Serrano <tom.serrano@elarahealth.com>
Cc: Elara Health Security <security@elarahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions from security review after demo

Tom —

Really appreciate the concise list. Below is a short, shareable summary we can use for the board packet; happy to expand any bullet into an appendix. Attaching: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf and a short support playbook.

Summary (short):
- PII scope: Redwood never persists unredacted PII in long-term customer blobs by default. Model inputs are processed in-memory/KV cache for inference; customers may opt to store transcripts for audit/analytics. When stored, they are encrypted at rest with customer or Redwood-managed KMS per contract.
- Retention: retention is configurable per-customer. Default log retention is 30 days; configurable windows include 30 / 90 / 365 / customer-managed S3.
- Residency: we support region pinning (hosted: us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1). For Elara, we can lock production workload to us-east-1 and disable cross-region backups (contract option).
- Support access & break-glass: support operates on least-privilege roles (support-readonly, support-troubleshoot). Break-glass is JIT: temporary elevated access granted via an internal ticket with two-step approval (owner + security) and expires automatically (default 30 minutes). All actions require MFA and generate an immutable audit trail.
- Logging & export: we provide request/response redaction toggles and can stream logs (audit + metrics) to customer SIEM via secure forwarders or deliver a daily S3 export.

Next steps / asks: 
1) Can you confirm whether the board needs the sample audit log (attached) or the full questionnaire answers?
2) If you want us to lock the workload to us-east-1, confirm and we will include the residency clause in the document.
3) I can schedule 30 min with Rishi (infra) and Marissa (contracts/ops) tomorrow for any technical/contract clarifications.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (summary), support-breach-playbook.docx (playbook)

Happy to iterate.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Laura / Marissa —

Quick technical confirmation and I'm attaching an example audit-log-sample.json for the board packet. Highlights: 

- Retention: defaults and options are: 30 days (default), 90 days, 365 days, or customer-managed S3 lifetime. Customer-managed S3 allows indefinite retention per the customer's lifecycle policies.
- KV / in-memory behavior: inference inputs are processed in memory; KV cache entries are ephemeral unless the customer opts into transcript persistence. Any persisted transcripts are encrypted with AES-256 and KMS.
- Break-glass & JIT access: implemented via our internal privilege bridge. Request must include ticket ID and business justification; two approvers (team owner + security) are required for production elevation. Elevation token is time-limited (configurable, default 30 minutes) and requires MFA. All elevated sessions are logged with operator, scope, timestamp, and reason.
- Audit exports: we support streaming to customer SIEM (Splunk/Datadog/ArcSight) over TLS, or daily S3 delivery with server-side encryption. The included audit-log-sample.json shows anonymized fields and the present schema.

I've attached: audit-log-sample.json (anonymized sample). Happy to run through a quick excerpt on the call.

— Rishi
